# 195 · A total wrong only for a quote no constructor makes, proved only on the quotes the constructor makes

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✓ Verified: preserved on every input of the stated domain, with nothing written by hand** | functional, no-false-positive | low | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`Pricing#total`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The value-object refactor of 190, with `total` returning a wrong amount for a quantity of zero or less, which `Quote`'s constructor refuses. The tool proves `total` preserved, and its result says over what: quotes made by their constructor, from any arguments it accepts. The bug is outside that claim, and the claim says it is.

Tags: [payments](../README.md#tag-payments), [special-values](../README.md#tag-special-values), [joint-run](../README.md#tag-joint-run), [object-inputs](../README.md#tag-object-inputs), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

`Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version `total` also returns `gross + 1` when `q.quantity <= 0`.

**Before** ([`Pricing.java`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java), line 1):

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        return quantity >= 10 ? gross / 10 : 0;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = q.cents * q.quantity;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }
```

**After:**

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel, over money. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more, written the other way round: the changed pure helper. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        if (quantity < 10) return 0;
        return gross / 10;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = q.amount.cents() * q.quantity;
        if (q.quantity <= 0) return gross + 1;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }
```

## What the verifier found

`shop.Pricing#total` is preserved: for every input of its domain the new build does what the old one did, as its claim observes it, under a relation nobody wrote.

The domain is `q: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts; in the previous version, a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from the new q's amount.cents and quantity as the correspondence's input equations say (old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents, old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity), and satisfying them`.

Every part the run checked, nothing written by hand (the entry points under their observation specs, each kernel pair under the correspondence alignment proposed), and what the rerun on the same proof cache took from the first run:

| Part | Kind | Verdict | On the rerun | Why not verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes` | entry point | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `POST /quotes/text` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `what the analysis can't see stays unresolved: the old build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled); the new build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled)` |
| `shop.Pricing#discount` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Pricing#total` | kernel | verified | an exact hit; `Pricing.discount` proved on its own and taken as one function |  |
| `shop.Pricing#withQuantity` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Money#cents (was shop.Quote#cents)` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `class not found in the previous version: shop.Money` |
| `shop.Quote#quantity` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `quantity is an instance method; a method of a record whose components are primitive is proved on the record's components, otherwise only static methods are` |

Obligations, one per observation of an old entry point: 7 preserved, 1 unresolved. Decisions a person made, by category: approved exclusion 0, domain restriction 0, environment assumption 0, mapping 0, observation change 0.

No question is left for a person.

What the verdicts rest on that nobody decided (assumed, not approved):

- KafkaTemplate.send is a recording stub in both builds: a recorded attempt is the call attempted, with its payload snapshotted at the call, not a delivery or a commit
- every modeled call returns normally, the environment model's only outcome: a failure of a store, broker or client is outside the claim
- QuotesController is made by its constructor with every dependency null and every other argument zero, in both builds: its dependencies are reached only through the modeled calls, and configuration it would be given is the type's default
- a payload string is snapshotted as the literal it is, among those of either build; any other string leaves the result unresolved
- at most 4 attempts are recorded, exactly in order; one more leaves the result unresolved

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`java -ea shop.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

A proof over objects has to make them somehow. Made by their constructors, they can't reach every state a field-by-field object could, so a bug only in such a state is not found, and a verdict that didn't say how its inputs were made would read as covering it.

## Why the verdict is right

The check makes each `Quote` by its constructor from symbolic arguments, and its domain label says exactly that: `a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts`, with the old version's quote made from the same values as the correspondence says. The constructor refuses a quantity below 1, so the new branch is never taken in the domain, and the verdict is verified within it, and claimed nowhere else.

## What to do

Nothing to fix for a quote made by its constructor. If a `Quote` can reach a quantity below 1 another way (`withQuantity` sets it without a check), the claim doesn't cover it: that is the label's point, and a domain of states after method calls is later work.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.
- The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the outside-domain defect (`defects/outside-domain/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.
- Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.
- What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and the instance method `Quote#quantity` (the regression check takes static methods, or a record's over its primitive components).
- Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `Pricing#total` verified, its domain naming the constructor; `POST /quotes`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.4 s cold, 0.2 s warm.
- `withQuantity(q, 0)` gives a quote that this `total` gets wrong, and nothing in the run says otherwise: the kernel's claims are each about one method over constructor-made inputs, not about sequences of calls.
- The app's tests pass on this version: the route makes every quote by the constructor.
